presentingComplaint: New fever, purulent sputum and worsening breathlessness on day 6 of a chemotherapy admission for acute myeloid leukaemia.
history: Admitted 6 days ago for induction chemotherapy (cytarabine + daunorubicin) for newly diagnosed AML. Profoundly neutropenic since day 4. Over the past 24 hours he has developed new fever to 39°C, increasingly purulent sputum and rising oxygen requirement, now needing 4 L/min nasal cannula having been on room air. He received a 3-day course of empirical piperacillin-tazobactam for a line-related fever two weeks earlier during a prior admission. No mechanical ventilation. No overt aspiration event witnessed. Not on chronic steroids beyond antiemetic dexamethasone. Non-smoker.
examination: Toxic-looking, in mild respiratory distress. Coarse crepitations and bronchial breathing over the right lower zone with reduced air entry at the right base. No oral thrush. Central line site clean and non-tender. No calf tenderness or unilateral leg swelling. Chest wall non-tender.
imaging: Portable CXR: new right lower and middle zone air-space consolidation not present on the admission film 6 days earlier; no cavitation, no effusion. Consistent with new nosocomial pneumonia arising >48h after admission.
microbiology: Two sets of peripheral and line blood cultures sent. Sputum Gram stain: numerous polymorphs (relatively few given neutropenia) with Gram-negative bacilli. Sputum and endotracheal-aspirate-equivalent deep respiratory sample sent for culture and sensitivities. Respiratory viral PCR and galactomannan sent to exclude alternative opportunistic pathogens. Culture at 48h: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, susceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime, meropenem, ciprofloxacin and amikacin; MRSA screen negative; galactomannan negative — enabling de-escalation from broad empiric cover to a single anti-pseudomonal agent.
differentialDiagnoses: Hospital-acquired (nosocomial) pneumonia — new consolidation >48h after admission in a neutropenic host
Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis / opportunistic fungal pneumonia (neutropenic host)
Undifferentiated febrile neutropenia without a focus
finalDiagnosis: Hospital-acquired pneumonia (right lower/middle lobe) due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a neutropenic AML patient
citations: IDSA/ATS Management of Hospital-acquired and Ventilator-associated Pneumonia 2016
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e — Pneumonia (Hospital-Acquired and Ventilator-Associated)
stewardship: Onset >48h after admission with new consolidation defines HAP. In a neutropenic host with a recent antibiotic course (MDR risk factor), start broad guideline-concordant empiric cover: an anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam (piperacillin-tazobactam or cefepime) plus a second anti-pseudomonal agent (amikacin) for double Gram-negative cover, plus vancomycin for MRSA given severity and prior antibiotic exposure. Obtain deep respiratory and blood cultures before/with the first dose. Once cultures return P. aeruginosa susceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam with a negative MRSA screen and negative galactomannan at 48h, de-escalate: stop vancomycin and the aminoglycoside and continue monotherapy with piperacillin-tazobactam. Reassess daily, use procalcitonin trend to support duration, and treat for a 7-day course provided clinical improvement.
contraindications: Avoid nephrotoxic aminoglycoside continuation once double cover is no longer needed, especially with any renal impairment
Vancomycin only while MRSA remains a possibility — discontinue on negative MRSA screen to limit selection pressure and AKI risk
Avoid unnecessary carbapenem escalation unless a resistant/ESBL organism is confirmed
edgeCases: Persistent fever/infiltrate despite appropriate antibacterials in a neutropenic host should trigger reassessment for invasive fungal disease (aspergillosis) with CT chest and antifungals
If the isolate had been MDR/carbapenem-resistant, escalation (e.g. ceftolozane-tazobactam or ceftazidime-avibactam) and infection-control isolation would be required rather than de-escalation
Neutropenia blunts the inflammatory response, so infiltrates and purulence may be subtle early and evolve as counts recover
expectedMaiK: New consolidation appearing >48h after hospital admission with purulent sputum and worsening oxygenation in a neutropenic patient is hospital-acquired pneumonia; empiric cover must be broad (anti-pseudomonal + MRSA) given MDR risk, then de-escalated to culture-directed monotherapy.
